sections.heading: This week
paragraphs: You have a cash problem before rent even lands. With ₦700k in hand and ₦4.6m due across rent, the loan app, and the supplier bill, the one thing that matters most this week is getting the landlord to accept part now with the rest later, before day 8 and the 9 days pass.

Your own figures also show the shop is already tight from day to day, so this is not only about this rent. If the money coming in and the costs stay where they are, the same gap will come back next month.

sections.heading: What's working
bullets: You still have steady trade from workers on lunch break, families around Surulere, and people who walk in or pass by.
You are already selling through calls, WhatsApp, and delivery apps, so people have more than one way to reach you.
You have handled split rent before. The landlord took half first and the rest later two years ago, so this is a real path to try again.

sections.heading: Pay attention to
bullets: The loan app repayment is due on day 8. Taking another loan to cover rent would just push the pressure forward and make the hole deeper.
Your own running costs add up to about ₦1.8m a month, while the money coming in looks like about ₦1.4m–₦1.8m a month. That means sales are not covering the costs you listed.
Prices have not changed for over a year, while diesel has almost doubled. That is likely squeezing every sale more than it looks.

sections.heading: Opportunity
paragraphs: The biggest opportunity is to buy time by getting the landlord to split the rent again, instead of letting a loan app eat more cash first. If that works, it protects the ₦700k you already have for the most urgent bill and keeps you from turning one due date into another bigger one.

At the same time, your normal day figure matters because it will tell you what this business can really carry. Right now, the number you mentioned about ₦2.5m a month does not match the day figures you gave, so I would work from the day numbers and use the bigger figure only if you can point to the months it came from.

sections.heading: Recommended actions
bullets: Call the landlord today and ask for part now, with the rest later. Mention you have paid this way before.
Stop any new loan app plan until the landlord answers.
Write down what the shop takes in for a normal day this week, from walk-ins, WhatsApp, calls, and delivery apps separately if you can.
Ask the supplier whether part payment can hold the account for now, so you do not lose supply while you sort the rent.

sections.heading: Something to send this week
paragraphs: [Landlord name], good day. I want to be straight with you: the rent of ₦3.6m is due in 9 days, and I am arranging what I can now. I have ₦700k in hand, and I want to pay part now and complete the rest later, the same way we handled it two years ago. Please let me know if I can bring the part payment today or tomorrow so we can agree the balance and date for the rest.

sections.heading: What would sharpen this
paragraphs: The two numbers worth noting this week are how much the landlord agrees to take now, and how many people actually pay after they ask or call. That tells you whether the immediate problem is the rent arrangement or the day-to-day cash coming through the shop.
Also keep the normal daily take separate from the ₦2.5m figure until you can show which months that came from. That will tell you whether the pressure is mainly price, costs, or slower trade.
